title: Parking & Waiting
whatItIs: Park where you won't put anyone in danger or block the way. Some of these rules are the law.

keyFacts.text: Before you leave the car you MUST switch off the engine, headlights and fog lights and apply the handbrake.

keyFacts: Don't park within 10 metres of a junction, except in an authorised parking space.

keyFacts.text: At night you MUST NOT park on a road facing against the traffic, unless in a recognised parking space.
On a road with a limit over 30 mph, you MUST use parking lights when parked at night.

keyFacts: Parking on a hill: uphill, turn the wheels away from the kerb; downhill, turn them towards it.

items.title: Within 10 m of a junction
items.text: Rule 243: not opposite or within 10 m of a junction, except in an authorised parking space.

items.title: Near a school entrance
items.text: Keep school entrance markings clear, even when picking up or setting down children.

items.title: Near a bus or tram stop
items.text: Don't stop or park at or near a bus or tram stop, or a taxi rank.

items.title: On a bend or hill brow
items.text: Also avoid the brow of a hill or a hump bridge (Rule 243).

items.title: At a lowered kerb
items.text: Lowered to help wheelchair users and powered mobility vehicles.

items.title: On zigzag lines
items.text: You MUST NOT stop or park on a crossing or on its zigzag lines.

b.label: Hazard warning lights
points: When stopped and temporarily blocking traffic

onTheTest.question: You park at night on a road with a 40 mph limit. What must you do?
onTheTest.why: On roads with a limit above 30 mph, vehicles parked at night must show parking lights.

traps: It is 10 metres from a junction, not 10 car lengths.
Hazard lights are not a licence to park where you shouldn't.
At night, park facing the same way as the traffic on your side.
